readOwner.belief: Ads are the next thing to buy. Not educated: the ads package and its $500 price were given before the $297 close, then "advanced SEO packages... social media marketing packages... all kinds of stuff" framed the offer as an agency menu. She bought the ads on the spot.
readOwner.did: "we sure do... our ads package is $500 package on top of your 297, okay? That's the campaign management side... keywords and anti-keywords" (24:38–24:59); "So we offer advanced SEO packages. We offer social media marketing packages. We have all kinds of stuff" (25:34).
readOwner.fix:
**Acknowledge (Q&A, "So you guys do Google Ads?"):** "We run ads and have in-depth SEO packages on the back end however we will never sell you on ads if you don't have your foundation set up. Most guys come to me thinking the first thing they have to do is run ads. That's like going from second gear to fourth gear without starting at first gear. If we sold you on ads, we'd be burning your money. First gear is your Google My Business listing and a website that actually turns the traffic into leads. Does that make sense?"
**Educate (Brandon's line C):** Our system works in synchronicity with that and actually helps your ads perform at a higher level, capturing more people and working them for you, turning every inquiry into a text conversation you pick up and close. Then the close stack and "which one do you want to get started with?"

readOwner.said: **30:00** "Let me just go back with you. The GMB Optimization, what does that mean again?"
readOwner.belief: The website and the listing are one thing. Partly: "that's where we're tagging the photos" named a finding, but the winning-formula frame was not re-said, so the $250 still had nothing of its own to stand on.
readOwner.did: "So that's where we're talking about the Google Optimization. So we are talking about your listing... that's where we're tagging the photos" (30:06–30:14).
readOwner.fix:
**Educate (Q&A, "Aren't you optimizing my listing when you build the site?"):** "Your website and your Google listing are two different assets, and Google ranks them separately. The $297 rebuilds and optimizes your website. Your Google Business Profile, the thing that shows up in the map pack, is its own optimization. The site supports the listing, but it won't fix a weak one on its own."
**Educate (Brandon's line J):** "There is a winning formula to get your listing set up the right way to increase your chances of ranking higher on the map pack, outside of us getting you reviews on our $297/month package."

readOwner.said: **30:53** "I'm looking at a company that, you know, I can continue and spend, you know, my digital presence." **31:20** "I want to understand, you know, your capability of this future together. So, campaign ads you're doing, Facebook, meta ads, you guys doing that too?"
readOwner.belief: A marketing company has to be the whole future, or it locks you in. Partly: "I'm not going to put you in a contract" was said, but the three numbers every month were not, so her reason to stay was "you love working with me" instead of the numbers.
readOwner.did: "We don't want to have you for three months and then you walk away... I'm not going to put you in a contract. I want you to stay with me because you love working with me, right?" (31:14–31:20); "No, we don't do meta ads currently... consumers are not engaging with businesses in automotive on social" (31:48), then the social funnels (32:05).
readOwner.fix:
**Educate (Script, the anchor line):** "The reason why people pay us $297 a month and we don't do contracts it's because we track three numbers every month so you can understand your ROI: leads captured from the traffic you're already getting, missed calls saved, reviews earned."
**Acknowledge (Q&A, "Can I keep doing Facebook?"):** "We focus on Google, because that's where people look for a shop. We don't run Yelp or Facebook. Keep doing Facebook if it's working for you. Just send those people to your new website instead of the DMs, so nothing gets lost and you can see every lead in one place."

readOwner.belief: The three months is the price of the extras, so the extras should be negotiable without it. Not educated: after "I can't do AI receptionist on that one" (36:30) the receptionist and the $250 listing were given on a one-month $797.
readOwner.did: "$2,391 for three months... the AI Receptionist for free, the Smart Website System, as well as the ads campaign, and the optimizations are free as well" (34:49); "$797 a month. But then you don't get your optimization and your AI Receptionist included" (35:21); "oh boy, oh boy... I will give you the GMB optimization at half price, and then I will include the AI receptionist. So I'm kind of giving you $400 more bucks" (37:05); "today's going to be $1,047 for everything" (37:41).
readOwner.fix:
**Acknowledge (Q&A, "Can I split the $891 over three months?"):** "I'll mark your account with my customer service team, and on the onboarding call they'll discuss how you want it split up."
**Educate (Script, 6, if he asks why three months):** "You're not going to change your business overnight. Month one we build everything and start reactivating your list. You'll see reviews coming in and, depending on how strong your listing already is, your first leads. Month two it's running. Month three is when you can actually look at the numbers and see what it's doing. Three months is a fair shot. Anything less and you're judging it before it's had a chance to work. And for giving it that shot, you get the listing at half off and the AI receptionist built specifically for your business, free. Still no contract — cancel any time after."

readOwner.said: **38:26** "The only thing, but you know, I need to notify these guys, you know... that I'm not going to work with them anymore." **41:15** "my husband just went out with a card... Just give me an hour."
readOwner.belief: She is ready; the vendor notice and the card are logistics. Yes: one week's notice tied to the launch week ("the week that we need to go live," "exactly"), checkout link by email, callback in one hour with the $250 authorized on that call.
